issues.description: The problem specification and template define a public method singFarmSong() in Farm (to print the song for all animals), but the reference solution implements this functionality under a different public method name playFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch between solution and the problem/template is structural and will confuse students and break tests that expect singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the public method name in the solution match the specification and template by renaming playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to the existing implementation. Ensure the Farm API in template, problem statement, and solution consistently uses singFarmSong().

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implementation exposes this functionality with a differently named public method playFarmSong(). This misalignment of the public API name for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and would cause code that calls singFarmSong() to fail against the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent method name across artifacts. Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (or conversely rename template/problem references to playFarmSong) so the public API matches the problem statement and template, ensuring students can map requirements to implementation and calls to singFarmSong() compile against the solution.
